campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 1, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered authorizing an agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority to accept low-carbon transportation program funding for a transit reliability and performance improvement project. The agenda also referenced pothole damage claims processes.
keyTopics: Resolution to authorize a low-carbon transportation and operations program fund agreement with VTA for a transit reliability improvement and performance systems project
Pothole damage claims process

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 2, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up routine business including approval of past meeting minutes, check registers, and the Treasurer's Report, along with responses to two Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole claims processing and VTA's oversight of BART Silicon Valley Phase II. The Council also considered a state bill on utility data transparency, a transportation impact fee study contract, forming a committee on alternative policing services, the future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival, and continued membership in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County.
keyTopics: Civil Grand Jury responses on pothole claims processing and VTA/BART Silicon Valley Phase II oversight
Support for AB 1761 on utility data transparency related to the Power Charge Indifference Adjustment
$85,000 contract with Fehr and Peers for a Transportation Impact Fee study
Forming an ad-hoc committee to review alternative policing services in Saratoga
Future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival and continued participation in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 8, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council took up a routine mix of budget, contract, and administrative items, including updated employee pay schedules, an increased contract for electrical maintenance services, and a proposed renaming of Lee Street to Tubman Street. The Council also considered restructuring a volunteer awards committee, forming a subcommittee for the City Manager's performance review, and discussed the Environmental Commission and a citizen initiative on zoning impacts.
keyTopics: Renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street
Amendment No. 4 with Bear Electrical Solutions increasing contract by $250,000
Revised Fiscal Year 2026/27 pay schedules for employee associations and unrepresented staff
Disbanding the joint Los Altos-Los Altos Hills Volunteer Awards Committee to form a Los Altos-only committee
Citizen initiative presentation on potential impacts to zoning

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 15, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine business at this meeting, including approval of minutes from prior meetings and the town's monthly financial and investment report for July 2026. The Council also considered several service agreements and contract amendments, including one related to heating, ventilation, and air conditioning work and multiple professional services agreements.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the September 1, 2026 Closed Session and regular Town Council meetings
Monthly Financial and Investment Report for July 2026
Amendment to a heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) services agreement
Professional services agreements for the Town Manager to execute

san-jose.title: San José City Council — September 15, 2026
san-jose.summary: The San José City Council considered a range of routine and policy items, including contracts for wastewater facility work, technology and security system agreements, and financial reporting for the past fiscal year. The agenda also included several housing and land-use matters, a proposed temporary moratorium on detention and custodial facilities on private property, and an update on the city's homelessness reduction efforts.
keyTopics: Temporary moratorium related to detention and custodial facilities on private property
Updated homelessness reduction work plan and functional zero model for FY 2026-2027
Housing and development items, including a tax/fee waiver for a Stevens Creek Blvd project and permits for sites at Cottle Road and Cozy Drive/Glider Drive
Zoning code amendment on reasonable accommodation (PP25-008)
Contract amendments covering wastewater facility construction contingency, a web content management system, and access control services

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — September 14, 2026
mountain-view.summary: Mountain View's Youth Advisory Committee met to hear public comments, take part in a team-building activity, and discuss its work plan for the upcoming fiscal year (2026-27). Committee members and staff also shared updates and comments on other city boards and committees.
keyTopics: Public oral communications on non-agenda items
Team-building exercise for committee members
Discussion of the Youth Advisory Committee's Fiscal Year 2026-27 work plan
Committee and staff comments and reports on other boards, commissions, and committees

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — September 15, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council considered routine business including a large equipment purchase, a road resurfacing contract, and a rejection of bids for the Plaza Del Sol Phase II project. The Council also took up a salary resolution for certain management employees, renaming the city's water pollution control plant, changes to its own meeting policies (including shifting the regular meeting start time to 6 p.m.), and a tax-exempt bond hearing for a 123-unit affordable housing project on Weddell Drive.
keyTopics: Purchase of a $793,417.50 combination jet/vacuum sewer cleaning truck for Environmental Services
Contract award for the Homestead Road Slurry Seal 2026 B paving project and rejection of all bids for Plaza Del Sol Phase II
Renaming the Donald M. Somers Water Pollution Control Plant to the Sunnyvale Donald M. Somers Clean Water Facility
Salary resolution increasing pay for Sunnyvale Managers Association and other management/confidential classifications
Council Policy Manual changes, including moving the regular Council meeting start time to 6 p.m.
TEFRA hearing and resolution on tax-exempt bonds for a 123-unit affordable rental housing project at 245 W. Weddell Drive

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 15, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council met to discuss potential litigation and a real property negotiation with the Cupertino Union School District regarding land at 10480 Finch Avenue, both in closed session. The public portion covered routine business including ordinance updates, an AI use policy for the Council, an ad-hoc committee for selecting a future city lobbyist, and a response to a county Civil Grand Jury report on pothole damage claims.
keyTopics: Closed session on anticipated litigation and real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue with Cupertino Union School District
Recognition of Cupertino High School students for their FBLA National Leadership Conference achievements
Adoption of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) City Council Policy
Response to the Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury report on pothole damage claims processes
Appointment of Mayor Moore and Councilmember Wang to a subcommittee evaluating city lobbyist proposals for 2027-2028

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council held a special meeting that began with interviews and appointments to fill two seats on the Civil Service Commission, followed by a joint session with the Stadium Authority Board. The joint meeting covered recognitions for outgoing board and commission members and campaign sponsors, along with routine business items including a janitorial services contract amendment, a historic preservation agreement, and annual board/commission workplans.
keyTopics: Interviews and appointment of two applicants to the Civil Service Commission
Recognition of outgoing commissioners from several city boards and the 2026 Mission Meets the Moment campaign sponsors
Contract amendment negotiations with Impec Group, Inc. for citywide janitorial services
Mills Act historical preservation agreement for the property at 1261 Jackson Street
Review of FY 2026-2027 annual workplans for city boards, commissions, and committees, plus designation of voting delegates for the League of California Cities

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered a range of items including federal community development grant funding, the city's red light camera safety program, and the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The Council also took up financial actions related to the former Redevelopment Agency's successor agency, including a bond refinancing measure.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution regarding the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Resolution for the sale and issuance of refunding bonds for the Successor Agency

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Planning & Transportation Commission — September 9, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Planning & Transportation Commission considered a proposed ordinance amending Palo Alto's zoning and subdivision codes to address City Council direction on allowing accessory dwelling units (ADUs) to be sold separately from the primary home. The Commission also heard a Director's Report covering upcoming meeting schedules and commissioner assignments, and was asked to approve draft minutes from its August 12, 2026 meeting.
keyTopics: Ordinance amending Municipal Code Titles 18 and 21 to permit separate sale of accessory dwelling units
Director's Report on meeting schedule and commissioner assignments
Approval of draft summary minutes from the August 12, 2026 meeting
